review.finding: Decision (a) makes re-baselining a maintainer decision if the benchmark rerun breaches the approved 5%/10% thresholds, yet the envelope record's verdict was 'No regression' and its awaiting list had no benchmark item. The comparison it made, head against the base binary, shows only that the slowdown predates this branch. Against the approved September 10 baseline the breach is confirmed in the baseline benchmark, for both binaries (all six controlled cold samples exceed 1.10x). Correction: in the public benchmark the gate run's single head sample (+12.2%) and the base binary's rerun median (+11.0%, 2 of 3 samples) breach, but the head's three rerun samples are below the approved baseline (-16.1% to -36.2%), so there the head's breach is not confirmed.
review.resolution: benchmark_breach below and an awaiting_maintainer item; README.md, CHANGELOG.md, RELEASE_GATES.md, and ARCHITECTURE_COMPATIBILITY.md (whose Qwen3.5 row repeated 'finds no regression') now say the breach is not attributable to this branch and awaits the maintainer. The envelope record stays byte-identical.

review.finding: README.md listed official base-model parity and NEMOTRON_H_ACCEPTANCE.md said the gate passes on 9a9c730, although it fails at f9f78b5 (cached decision 22 at 0.998558 against the 0.998635 floor) and the failure stands at 8181605.
review.resolution: Both say the gate passed at 9a9c730 and fails at f9f78b5 (and so at 8181605), attributed to the once-rounded Mamba-2 convolution SiLU, pending review of the floor rule, and link the envelope record; NEMOTRON_H_ACCEPTANCE.md's comparison and remaining-gates sections too.

review.finding: No test reached the Mamba-2 or Gated DeltaNet convolution SiLU call site; putting activation::silu back in either mixer failed nothing.
review.resolution: convolution_silu_is_rounded_once_in_half_precision in src/mamba2_tests.rs and src/delta_net_tests.rs read the post-convolution activation exactly through the F32 recurrent state (identity convolutions, exact unit factors), in BF16, F16 (equal to the F32 SiLU rounded once, unequal to the composed graph on separating probes; BF16 2.8125 gives 2.65625, not 2.640625) and F32 (bit-identical to activation::silu), in both scan modes. Reverting each call site fails its test (mutations).

review.verdict: confirmed; the test exposed a graph defect, fixed
review.finding: Only the eager score scale and the fused output were pinned. The requested emulation (Q K^T summed in F32 and rounded, the unrounded scale in F32, the mask and bias add in the dtype, an F32 softmax rounded once, P V summed in F32 and rounded) matched Burn's eager graph in BF16 but not in F16 on Flex: 10 of 120 probabilities and 45 of 96 outputs differed, because Burn Flex 0.21's F16 GEMM keeps F16 partial sums.
review.resolution: The graph, not a tolerance, was fixed: on inference Flex the eager graph forms its two F16 products from F32 operands and rounds once (f32_accumulated_matmul). The new test half_precision_eager_attention_rounds_like_transformers_eager compares probabilities and outputs with the emulation bit for bit on grouped heads with a causal mask, a fully masked row, and a bias, and the outputs with Transformers 5.2.0's own eager_attention_forward (pinned bits); four variants show the grid detects each alternative rounding. Metal's F16 products are F32 sums rounded once and Metal's eager graph equals Transformers' eager on the grid (ignored Metal tests), so Metal is unchanged.

review.finding: muse_attention_precision selects the eager graph for F16 and BF16, so the eager-scale change altered Muse-Glimmer's default half-precision numerics (128-wide heads); GPT-2 also defaults to eager, where 64-wide heads make the scale an exact 1/8. CHANGELOG.md said 'the fused default path is unaffected', and ARCHITECTURE_COMPATIBILITY.md attributed Muse's f9f78b5 statistics to the SiLU change alone. The envelope record's not_run entry for gpt-oss also says the eager graph is one 'which no real-checkpoint gate selects', which is wrong for Muse-Glimmer-30B's official gate.
review.resolution: CHANGELOG.md and RELEASE_GATES.md name Muse-Glimmer's half-precision default and GPT-2 and GPT-NeoX (a no-op where the scale is a power of two) as eager-graph users; the Muse rows attribute 0.999931849 (against 0.999943377 at c15f24e) to both changes, which no control separates. The envelope record stays byte-identical; this entry corrects it.

review.finding: The gate-level refusal of TRANSFORMERS_GEMMA_DTYPE=f16 and the dropped Metal/F16 profile belong to stage S7, held until the maintainer confirms decision (d); it hid the measured outcome of decision (b, F16): an uncalibrated envelope.
review.resolution: load_bundle no longer refuses f16; an F16 run reads TRANSFORMERS_GEMMA_F16_OFFICIAL_DIRS and _LONG_F16_OFFICIAL_DIRS and fails as uncalibrated before loading (all five Metal runs here). The docs say Gemma F16 is uncalibrated (all official F16 graphs overflow) and leave the refusal to decision (d); S7 can reinstate it.

review.finding: No committed log measured PyTorch's scalar multiply; probe_half.log measured only Burn against an emulation labelled PyTorch.
review.resolution: probes/probe_torch_half.log: on the CPU, x * (1/sqrt(128)) with a Python float equals the F32 product rounded once on all 65,280 finite BF16 and 63,488 finite F16 values; on MPS all F16 agree and 1,120 BF16 values differ, each an F32 product in the subnormal range flushed to zero (1,118 would round to a BF16 subnormal, 2 to the smallest normal). The docstring cites the log and names the convention as the CPU's.

benchmark_breach.policy: BENCHMARKS.md: performance changes above 5% alert; a greater-than-10% regression fails only after a controlled rerun confirms it on the same benchmark series. The approved baseline is the September 10 controlled measurements (v0_1-release-20260910.json, user_authorized_rebaseline).

decision_source.quote: If the benchmark rerun breaches the approved 5%/10% thresholds, re-baselining becomes a maintainer decision.

benchmark_breach.verdict: The cold first token breaches the approved baseline in both benchmarks' gate runs; the controlled rerun confirms the breach in the baseline benchmark for both binaries, and in the public benchmark for the base binary, not the head. The base binary 7bd057e shows it too, so the slowdown predates this branch and is not attributable to it (the head's medians are below the base's, ratios 0.813 and 0.743). Whether to re-baseline is a maintainer decision; nothing is re-baselined or waived here.
benchmark_breach.supersedes: the envelope record's benchmarks.verdict ('No regression'), which judged the head against the base binary only; that record stays byte-identical

awaiting_maintainer.item: Re-baselining Qwen3.5-0.8B's cold first token: it breaches the approved September 10 baseline in both benchmarks, in the base binary 7bd057e as well as the head (benchmark_breach); the slowdown predates this branch. Until then the breach stands and no baseline changes.

The Gemma 3 F16 policy: a library-level default refusal with an explicit opt-in (a family-declared range hazard checked by a generic LoadOptions policy), and the gate changes the decision lists (refuse TRANSFORMERS_GEMMA_DTYPE=f16, drop a Metal/F16 Gemma profile). This round withdrew the gate-level refusal; until the decision, Gemma f16 runs fail as uncalibrated.
A Burn >= 0.22 upgrade (MSRV 1.92 -> at least 1.95, the backend-erased Tensor API), the only route found to Metal BF16; Burn 0.21 keeps the contextual refusal.
A reviewed rule for the Nemotron-H official-precision floors (each path's worst official F16 row), which the once-rounded Mamba-2 SiLU misses at cached decision 22; nothing was tuned.
A non-finite guard in generation, and a post-attention-add hook (v0.2 interface).
Gemma 3 1B/270m and Gemma 2 checkpoints for F16 measurements.
